commit message:
Tensorflow Layer (TFLayer) added (#108)

* Tensorflow Layer (TFLayer) added

Main files of importance for TFLayer to work: interface_tf.py, tequila/__init__.py, ml/__init__.py, ml_api.py, objective.py

Why the changes in objective.py? When calling extract_variables() on a VectorObjective, the list returned is unordered, which later on caused problems assigning variables to their respective values. Also, to sort them, __lt__() had to be implemented, so the simplest way I saw to order them was by name.

Other files changed to allow sampling: simulator_base.py (only removed "assert n_samples == samples" on line 441 due to problems when using simulators like simulator_cirq.py, which filtered the count value and made the assertion fail)

Files added for testing: test_tf_interface.py

* objective.py compares variables by hash of the names. Also, more tests added and adjusted the preamble in interface_torch.py since I modified preamble to sort the extracted variables and to return input_vars which in turn allowed mapping the variables to the values more easily.

Finally, HAS_TORCH and HAS_TF has been modified in terms of desired way of access per Jakob's request.

* Adjusted interface_tf.py to use self.first and self.second for ordering the values in the self.input_variable and self.params_variable. Essentially, a better way of mapping.

* Fixed test_torch_interface.py

* Reinserted failsafe

Co-authored-by: brandon <100405959@alumnos.uc3m.es>

Addition of techniques from https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2023-01-03-889 (Izmaylov Group)
PR authored by: Seonghoon Choi and Aranya Chakraborty 

* Completed SVD (commit on behalf of Aranya Chakraborty).
* Completed FFF (commit on behalf of Aranya Chakraborty).
* Improved the efficiency of F3.
* Truncated CISD containing only a few slater determinant terms is usedinstead of the full CISD.
* F3 is performed only on a few large variance fragments.
* Safer choice of minimum meas_alloc (1e-6) to avoid issues with allocating 0 shots.
* Addressing minor comments.
* Adding tests for Fermionic measurement optimization schemes.
* Returning rotated (cartan form) obt and tbts after F3.
* Changed OSI to ICS for consistency.

* Circuit for fermionic measurement techniques:
* Added circuit implementations of orbital rotations
* Added test for orbital rotations.

* Proper handling of non-symmetric fermionic Hamiltonian (happens when one obtains it from reverse_jordan_wigner of a qubit Hamiltonian).
* Handling options in compile_groups to better deal with exceptions and
  default options.
* get_fermionic_wise now correctly returns QubitHamiltonian rather than
  openfermion QubitOperator.
* If suggested samples = 0, at least 1 sample (shot) is allocated for
  that measurable fragment.

* Removed trailing whitespaces.
* Removed unused variables.

- QASM 3 import and advanced symbolic expression support are not yet implemented.

Tensorflow Layer (TFLayer) added

Main files of importance for TFLayer to work: interface_tf.py, tequila/__init__.py, ml/__init__.py, ml_api.py, objective.py

commit message:
Pr overlap groups (#255)

* Implemented sorted insertion grouping.

* Sorted insertion grouping (a type of greedy grouping method)
has been implemented for both qubit wise commuting and fully
commuting groups.
* Added tests to verify that sorted insertion grouping returns
appropriately commutative groups.

* Implementation of overlapping sorted insertion (coefficient splitting).

* Introduced class OverlappingGroups for initializing the mutually
commuting fragments with overlapping coefficients and for optimizing
these coefficients (according to cov_dict).
* Added tests for the newly added OverlappingGroups.
* Implemented __eq__ in BinaryPauliString and added a corresponding test.

* Addressed comments by Thomson (tymcr).

* Passing options from top-level down to commuting_groups.

* Implementation of suggested sample size.

* If one wishes to evaluate commuting groups using the suggested sample
  size, it can be done by specifying samples="auto-total#ofsamples",
  e.g., samples="auto-1000000" when compiling the objective (or
  circuit).
* Currently, suggested samples require a covariance dictionary.
  However, in the future, automatic evaluation of covariances will be
  implemented.

* Bugfix: Overlapping did not consider new Paulis.

* Pauli products can only be introduced to a fragment when it commutes
  with all elements. However, the commutativity with the newly
  introduced Paulis were not considered. This commit fixes the bug.
* Added ignore_const in init_from_qubit_hamiltonian such that we do not
  waste computation effort coefficient splitting the constant term.

* Addressing comments from kottmanj.

Authored-by: Seonghoon Choi <seonghoon.choi@epfl.ch> thanks to Thomson Yen @tymcr  for feedback

commit message:
Pr measurement optim f3 (#281)

Improvement on Measurement Optimization:
Addition of techniques from https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2023-01-03-889 (Izmaylov Group)
PR authored by: Seonghoon Choi and Aranya Chakraborty 

* Completed SVD (commit on behalf of Aranya Chakraborty).
* Completed FFF (commit on behalf of Aranya Chakraborty).
* Improved the efficiency of F3.
* Truncated CISD containing only a few slater determinant terms is usedinstead of the full CISD.
* F3 is performed only on a few large variance fragments.
* Safer choice of minimum meas_alloc (1e-6) to avoid issues with allocating 0 shots.
* Addressing minor comments.
* Adding tests for Fermionic measurement optimization schemes.
* Returning rotated (cartan form) obt and tbts after F3.
* Changed OSI to ICS for consistency.

* Circuit for fermionic measurement techniques:
* Added circuit implementations of orbital rotations
* Added test for orbital rotations.

* Proper handling of non-symmetric fermionic Hamiltonian (happens when one obtains it from reverse_jordan_wigner of a qubit Hamiltonian).
* Handling options in compile_groups to better deal with exceptions and
  default options.
* get_fermionic_wise now correctly returns QubitHamiltonian rather than
  openfermion QubitOperator.
* If suggested samples = 0, at least 1 sample (shot) is allocated for
  that measurable fragment.

* Removed trailing whitespaces.
* Removed unused variables.

---------

Co-authored-by: Aranya Chakraborty <aranyac@iisc.ac.in>
Co-authored-by: Seonghoon Choi <seonghoon.choi@utoronto.ca>
Co-authored-by: J. S. Kottmann <jakob.kottmann@gmail.com>

called, then it monkey patches the safe.get_defaults to use 
safe_qgis.get_defaults
to do this I had refactored defaults to its own file to avoid a __init__ 
cascade that was loading the inpact function before safe_qgis.__init__
could monkeypatch the get defaults method.

this fixes #704 and probably all the related QPainter issues

commit message:
Merge changes from release to master (#5078)

* use the official QGIS docker base image for travis

* Fix relative root location of Makefile for pep test.

* skip windows flake8 check, review print, move up get_qgis_app

* enable QGIS 3.4 on travis

* disable OSM Reporter

* improve error message when reports are not going to be generated

* update local docker test configuration

* Fix contour calculation in QGIS 3.4

Related with issue #5063
Switch contour generation to use geopackage driver, following
QGIS default options.
It will force contour to have Linestring geometry instead of
randomly becomes MultiLinestring.

* Fix inconsistent aggregation behaviour

Aggregated numbers can be slightly different
due to different combination of hazard,aggregation
being matched with exposure.
Attempt to make the behaviour consistent by sorting
the aggregate hazard first before comparing it with
exposure.

* Fix and enable skipped unittests

Enable previously skipped unittests.
Previous test were disabled due to
inconsistent behaviour.
This was fixed.

* Maintenance commit for repo

- Assign default python-version for pyenv
- Pin package version in REQUIREMENTS_TESTING.txt
- Update run-env-linux.sh
- Fix new flake issues

* Fix typo and null error

* Change contour shp extension to gpkg in unittest

* Skip test_contour unit test in QGIS 3.4

Skip safe.gis.raster.test.test_contour unit test
in QGIS 3.4. This is due the qgis_testrunner.sh thread
was stalling. The stalling code is inside qgis binary,
so I decided that we won't further debug the problem.

The unit test can be run directly with unittest
without problem.

* Enable minimum needs unit test

* Skip stalling unit tests in QGIS 3.4

* Skip some tests

* Fix hazard preparation geometries

Fix #5074

After polygonized, the hazard layer needs its geometries fixed.
We do that using qgis processing alg.

* Fix scenario unit test files

Related with fix #5074

* change clipping dtype to be the same as input

* Fix minimum needs value report

* Update release metadata to 5.0.1

* Fix and streamline unit tests

commit message:
Fix test failure on master builds

The handling of geojson files has changed in qgis master, causing
fields to be loaded again after commit the layer's changes. But
because there's no values present in the new field, there's nothing
in the resultant geojson file to maintain this newly added field,
and it's lost when reloading from disk.

commit message:
Windspeed  (#4133)

* Update cyclone hazard classification notes

* Displacement rates for SSHWS categories

Displacement rates for Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale have been
copied from Australian BoM classification, but threshold wind speeds for
the categories are different.

* generate map report in IFCW too

* enable inasafe for QGIS 2.14, 2.16 and 2.18

* add missing notes for EQ impact function

* review comments in hazard.py

* Standardise wind speed averaging times

Updated the scales to use a standard wind speed averaging time period of
0.2 seconds. Conversions are based on the WMO Technical Guideline 1555
(Harper et al., 2010:
http://www.wmo.int/pages/prog/www/tcp/documents/WMO_TD_1555_en.pdf),
assuming "Off-sea" conditions (i.e. wind speeds are representative of
over-land wind speeds, close to the coast where the wind is blowing off
the sea), and a reference time of 600 seconds.

Conversion factors can be calculated using the IPython Notebook at
https://github.com/wcarthur/notebooks/blob/master/Wind%20speed%20averaging%20conversions.ipynb

* Update .gitmodules to use https

I've had problems accessing the `parameters` submodule from behind our proxy. Tried to use ssh instead (but that was unsuccessful as well). This caused the Travis CI check to fail

* PEP8 fix

commit message:
Standardise wind speed averaging times

Updated the scales to use a standard wind speed averaging time period of
0.2 seconds. Conversions are based on the WMO Technical Guideline 1555
(Harper et al., 2010:
http://www.wmo.int/pages/prog/www/tcp/documents/WMO_TD_1555_en.pdf),
assuming "Off-sea" conditions (i.e. wind speeds are representative of
over-land wind speeds, close to the coast where the wind is blowing off
the sea), and a reference time of 600 seconds.

Conversion factors can be calculated using the IPython Notebook at
https://github.com/wcarthur/notebooks/blob/master/Wind%20speed%20averaging%20conversions.ipynb

commit message:
Handle building categories correctly with QGIS layers

If impact function works directly with QGIS layers, attributes
with NULL value are represented by QPyNullVariant instances
instead of being None.

This addition makes sure that QPyNullVariant objects are
not propagated to reporting code, which only expects None
for NULL values.

Without this, user gets Python errors when writing reports
as the code tries to treat those values as regular strings.

commit message:
Optimize flooding raster/road impact function

Summary of the changes:
- instead of polygonization of the flood map (which create very complex polygons),
  now we create a temporary layer where each cell is a separate rectangular polygon
- only flooded cells are created in the temporary layer... fewer geometries
  to create and process later
- flood vector layer is spatially indexed for fast spatial lookups
- for each road, we first query flood rectangles within the bounding box
  of the road, then assemble a minimal flood polygon in that area
  (roads are typically small, so not much work to do)
- finally for each road we do geoprocessing with its flood polygon:
   1. intersection - what is flooded
   2. difference - what is not flooded
  (these are done on small/simple geometries so they are fast to produce results)

In my local tests with Jakarta roads from OSM and 2007 flood raster,
the speedup is ~20x for the splitting into flooded / not flooded roads.

* Merge changes from release to master (#5078)

* use the official QGIS docker base image for travis

* Fix relative root location of Makefile for pep test.

* skip windows flake8 check, review print, move up get_qgis_app

* enable QGIS 3.4 on travis

* disable OSM Reporter

* improve error message when reports are not going to be generated

* update local docker test configuration

* Fix contour calculation in QGIS 3.4

Related with issue #5063
Switch contour generation to use geopackage driver, following
QGIS default options.
It will force contour to have Linestring geometry instead of
randomly becomes MultiLinestring.

* Fix inconsistent aggregation behaviour

Aggregated numbers can be slightly different
due to different combination of hazard,aggregation
being matched with exposure.
Attempt to make the behaviour consistent by sorting
the aggregate hazard first before comparing it with
exposure.

* Fix and enable skipped unittests

Enable previously skipped unittests.
Previous test were disabled due to
inconsistent behaviour.
This was fixed.

* Maintenance commit for repo

- Assign default python-version for pyenv
- Pin package version in REQUIREMENTS_TESTING.txt
- Update run-env-linux.sh
- Fix new flake issues

* Fix typo and null error

* Change contour shp extension to gpkg in unittest

* Skip test_contour unit test in QGIS 3.4

Skip safe.gis.raster.test.test_contour unit test
in QGIS 3.4. This is due the qgis_testrunner.sh thread
was stalling. The stalling code is inside qgis binary,
so I decided that we won't further debug the problem.

The unit test can be run directly with unittest
without problem.

* Enable minimum needs unit test

* Skip stalling unit tests in QGIS 3.4

* Skip some tests

* Fix hazard preparation geometries

Fix #5074

After polygonized, the hazard layer needs its geometries fixed.
We do that using qgis processing alg.

* Fix scenario unit test files

Related with fix #5074

* change clipping dtype to be the same as input

* Fix minimum needs value report

* Update release metadata to 5.0.1

* Fix and streamline unit tests

commit message:
Make flood vector-building impact function faster

This is done by using spatial index to identify which flood polygons
will need exact intersection test (much faster than doing intersection
with one huge polygon)

A small extra optimization is to write features in batches as that is
more efficient than writing features one by one.

Measured speed improvement on Jakarta test data (2013 flood polygons
and OSM buildings) was ~40x (from 30min down to 40sec)

Refactor how notes are handled (#3023)

* Fix #2973 - explain about rounding used in presented reports. Fix issue introduced by #2845 which added invalid notes to generic landcover IF. Fixed issue in generic landcover IF which was not inheriting the mixin and thus failing to render the notes properly. Moved floods.shp test data to jk so it intersects with landcover.
* Updated all impact functions to include notes helper from impact function base and return a list of notes rather than a dict
* Added readme for JSON examples
* Move more actions into definitions.py and add hazard based actions to all IFs
* More DRY for actions - implement actions and notes and IF base class and use standard form for creating them unless an IF needs special behaviour.
* Added actions method to mixin base
* Fix failing tests resulting from notes and actions refactoring. Other cleanups to tests
* Refactor unit test for test_tsunami_landcover so that tests pass and are easily comparable with dock values
* Use almost equal for tsunami on landcover test so that it works on different platforms
* Fix for travis test with tsunami landcover

commit message:
Fix test failure on master builds

The handling of geojson files has changed in qgis master, causing
fields to be loaded again after commit the layer's changes. But
because there's no values present in the new field, there's nothing
in the resultant geojson file to maintain this newly added field,
and it's lost when reloading from disk.

author: Alessandro Pasotti <elpaso@itopen.it>
commit message:
QGIS/Qt5 API Changes

This is a blob of API updates, sorry if it's not atomic

- Py3 "in" instead of "has_key" when checking a dict
- QGIS QgsVectorFileWriter requires a QgsCoordinateTransform (even if empty)
- QGIS uri.setNameFilters takes a list
- Py3 assertItemsEqual is gone, using an in-house implementation (dict_value_sorted) or just compare the dicts
- QGIS more geometry -> constGet leftovers
- Qt5 setResizeMode -> setSectionResizeMode,
- Qt5 QtGui -> QtWidgets
- Qt5 qApp/QCoreApplication/QApplication mix -> QgsApplication
- QGIS QgsGeometry.exportToWkt() -> asWtk()
- QGIS QgsMapLayerProxyModel is now in core
- QGIS QgsApplication.qgisUserDbFilePath() -> qgisUserDatabaseFilePath()
- QGIS removed unneded canvas.hasCrsTransformEnabled()
- Qt qWaitForWindowShown -> qWaitForWindowExposed

QGIS2 and QGIS3 zonal stats results.

commit message:
QGIS/Qt5 API Changes

This is a blob of API updates, sorry if it's not atomic

- Py3 "in" instead of "has_key" when checking a dict
- QGIS QgsVectorFileWriter requires a QgsCoordinateTransform (even if empty)
- QGIS uri.setNameFilters takes a list
- Py3 assertItemsEqual is gone, using an in-house implementation (dict_value_sorted) or just compare the dicts
- QGIS more geometry -> constGet leftovers
- Qt5 setResizeMode -> setSectionResizeMode,
- Qt5 QtGui -> QtWidgets
- Qt5 qApp/QCoreApplication/QApplication mix -> QgsApplication
- QGIS QgsGeometry.exportToWkt() -> asWtk()
- QGIS QgsMapLayerProxyModel is now in core
- QGIS QgsApplication.qgisUserDbFilePath() -> qgisUserDatabaseFilePath()
- QGIS removed unneded canvas.hasCrsTransformEnabled()
- Qt qWaitForWindowShown -> qWaitForWindowExposed

commit message:
QGIS/Qt5 API Changes

This is a blob of API updates, sorry if it's not atomic

- Py3 "in" instead of "has_key" when checking a dict
- QGIS QgsVectorFileWriter requires a QgsCoordinateTransform (even if empty)
- QGIS uri.setNameFilters takes a list
- Py3 assertItemsEqual is gone, using an in-house implementation (dict_value_sorted) or just compare the dicts
- QGIS more geometry -> constGet leftovers
- Qt5 setResizeMode -> setSectionResizeMode,
- Qt5 QtGui -> QtWidgets
- Qt5 qApp/QCoreApplication/QApplication mix -> QgsApplication
- QGIS QgsGeometry.exportToWkt() -> asWtk()
- QGIS QgsMapLayerProxyModel is now in core
- QGIS QgsApplication.qgisUserDbFilePath() -> qgisUserDatabaseFilePath()
- QGIS removed unneded canvas.hasCrsTransformEnabled()
- Qt qWaitForWindowShown -> qWaitForWindowExposed

Remove some tests for MPI functions and constants

As PnetCDF requires MPI-IO which was first introduced in MPI 2,
we can simply check MPI_VERSION defined in all mpi.h to skip
tests for MPI functions and constants introduced in MPI 2.
Check for deprecated MPI functions and constants are only needed
when the supplied MPI libraries support MPI 3 and later, i.e.
those functions and constants may be still defined in the libraries.

commit message:
Fix errors when building an RPM

Building an RPM for OpenHPC of pnetcdf fails with:

```
+ /usr/lib/rpm/check-buildroot
/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0/bin/pnetcdf-config:prefix=/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0
/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0/bin/pnetcdf-config:exec_prefix=/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0
/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0/lib/pkgconfig/pnetcdf.pc:prefix=/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0
/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0/lib/pkgconfig/pnetcdf.pc:exec_prefix=/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64/opt/ohpc/pub/libs/gnu14/mvapich2/pnetcdf/1.14.0
Found '/home/ohpc/rpmbuild/BUILDROOT/pnetcdf-gnu14-mvapich2-ohpc-1.14.0-19999.ci.ohpc.x86_64' in installed files; aborting
```

The reason is that the variable DESTDIR is added to the path of the
binary location. This is, however, wrong. DESTDIR is the directory where
the files are installed but not where they are located in the final
RPM.

Keeping DESTDIR for the file location is correct but not for the path
where the files are located.

With this patch applied, it is possible to create an RPM without errors
like above.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com>

runs.  Its purpose is for comparing performance of NetCDF4 against PnetCDF,
when running on one process. Note pnetcdf_put_vara.c has options of using
blocking and nonblocking APIs.  When using the blocking APIs, its write call
sequence is exactly the same as netcdf_put_vara.c. Thus, the comparison should
be fair.

commit message:
ad-hoc configure settings for NAG Fortran

1. NAG Fortran 6.2 and earlier has no command-line option to show the
   flags needed to verbose linking output. Such flags are important for
   linking C and Fortran libraries. According to autoconf user guide,
   the call to AC_F77_LIBRARY_LDFLAGS should set such flags in variable
   ac_cv_prog_f77_v. Because NAG Fortran lacks of such feature, the
   variable is set to empty. This commit hard codes the variable to
   "-Wl,-v". Note setting ac_cv_prog_f77_v="-Wl,-v" must appear before
   the call to AC_F77_LIBRARY_LDFLAGS
2. Similar fix for ac_cv_prog_fc_v.
3. Add -Wc=$MPICC to FFLAGS and FCFLAGS to force NAG Fortran to use the
   same CC (e.g. gcc) version as the one used to build MPICC. Without
   this fack, NAG Fortran may use a different CC.
4. Revise UD_CHECK_MPIF90_IS_NAG in acinclude.m4
5. Add UD_CHECK_MPIF77_IS_NAG in acinclude.m4

commit message:
Replace use of PATH_MAX with MPI_MAX_INFO_VAL

Burst buffer directory name is passed from an MPI hint and the argument
"value" of MPI_Info_get() is limited to the size of MPI_MAX_INFO_VAL.
The default of PATH_MAX is 4096. This value can be bigger than
MPI_MAX_INFO_VAL and thus we cannot use PATH_MAX.

For MPICH, the the default value of MPI_MAX_INFO_VAL is 1024, which
cannot be changed even at configure time.

For OpenMPI, the default value of MPI_MAX_INFO_VAL is 256, but can
be changed at configure time through command-line option
--with-max-info-val=VALUE.

commit message:
Bugs fixed to pass most tests in "nc_test":

1.
I didn't include "BYTE" datatype support in the parallel implementation, while
the nc_test DOES require this and expect type-related errors in the test. Now,
I've added this kind of support.

2.
Some of the error codes are not catched in ncmpi, while nc_test DOES expect the correct codes in time of specific errors. I've fixed them.

3.
nc_test is tightly connected with the authors' serial netCDF implementation
code. Most FAILURE in our test is due to "incorrect" test.nc file which is
generated by nc_test itself. In serial nc_test, the authors assume if some
error (e.g. datatype range error) happens, the (overflowed) data is still
written into file, while in the parallel netCDF implementation, I chose to
abort with the error code returned. I've changed it to follow the same rule
to satisfy nc_test.

4. [FATAL]
The type conversion between int and float is incorrect in ncmpi implementation. I've fixed it.

5.
In time of multi-errors, the serial netcdf check these errors in a different
sequential order than ncmpi implementation, while nc_test assumes and expects
the former. I've changed it to follow the same order to satisfy nc_test.

6.
Some special-case errors were not detected and make nc_test crash, e.g.
MPI_Type_create_subarray crashes when 0-subsize is specified.

commit message:
= PnetCDF file header synchronization mechanism =

== Synchronize header data cached in memory ==

1. Changes to attributes, names of variables and dimensions
The following APIs can modify file header while being called in data mode. Note that these APIs can only modify existing attributes, rename variables or dimensions, given that the new attributes and names do not take more file space than the old ones. Otherwise, these APIs are prohibited in data mode.

    ncmpi_rename_dim(),
    ncmpi_rename_var(),
    ncmpi_copy_att(),
    ncmpi_rename_att(), and
    ncmpii_put_att_<type>()

The above semantics implemented in PnetCDF conform with the netCDF for the corresponding APIs. However, since PnetCDF is designed to handle parallel I/O to shared files, it must ensure data consistency for the file header that is cached in the memory of all MPI processes.  In order to do so, PnetCDF requires the above APIs to be called collectively and use the same argument values while in data mode.  PnetCDF does not automatically check the argument consistency, unless the program is in safe mode, i.e. the environment variable PNETCDF_SAFE_MODE is set to 1. Consistency checking requires one or more MPI collective communication operations, a cost some users may want to avoid.  Please note that the above consistency issue is about the file header data that is cached in the memory. For committing the head changes to the file, see below.

2. Changes to the number of records
At the end of collective put APIs that write record variables, PnetCDF synchronizes the number of records across all processes. This memory synchronization is enforced even if the program is not in the safe mode.  On the other hand for independent APIs, the number of records is not automatically synchronized, as memory synchronization requires MPI collective communication calls. Users are encouraged to call ncmpi_sync_numrecs() to explicitly synchronize the number of records. Note this new API is collective, but can be called in the independent data mode. Number of records is stored in the file header. For committing the number of records to the file, please see below.

== Commit header changes to file ==
In PnetCDF, only root process (rank 0) can write/read/modify the file header.  Thus, committing the changes to file header is done through the root. Before writing to file header, PnetCDF checks the consistency of header data cached in memory across MPI processes.  However, PnetCDF does not commit the header changes immediately to the file, unless the file is opened/created in NC_SHARE mode. If NC_SHARE is not set, the changes to the header data will be cached in memory and flushed to the file when calling ncmpi_close().

If you expect your PnetCDF program to be interrupted or exit in between a file open and close (due to returned error codes or system cash) and wish the file contains most up-to-date metadata (e.g. number of records), NC_SHARE mode should be used.

commit message:
This commit is the first cut of supporting thread safety.
A pthread mutex is added in the following two files to protect global variables
and thread unsafe subroutine calls.
1. There are 3 global variables defined in src/dispatchers/file.c that need to
   be protected by mutex:
       static PNC *pnc_filelist[NC_MAX_NFILES];
       static int  pnc_numfiles;
       static int  ncmpi_default_create_format;
2. The binary tree used by tfind()/tsearch()/tdelete() cannot be updated safely
   in the multi-threading environment. Thus, calling these subroutines is
   protected by a mutex.

A test C program test/testcase/tst_pthread.c and an example C program
examples/C/pthread.c are added to test the one-file-per-thread I/O operations.

Note that this commit was only tested with the one-file-per-thread case. More
test cases will be added later.

commit message:
This revision is mainly to support the new data types introduced in CDF-5
specification: UBYTE, USHORT, UINT, INT64, and UINT64

1. Support the following CDF-5 data types for C APIs:
   unsigned short, unsigned int, 64-bit integer (int64), unsigned int64
   New APIs: ncmpi_put_vara_ushort(), ncmpi_put_vara_uint(),
             ncmpi_put_vara_longlong(), and ncmpi_put_vara_ulonglong(), etc.

2. Support the following CDF-5 data types for Fortran APIs:
   64-bit integer (int8)
   New APIs: nfmpi_put_vara_int8(), etc.

3. The new APIs follow the looks of netCDF4.

4. Extend test program, nc_test and nf_test, to test the new data types.
   Note that for data types int64 and uint64, test for out-of-bound values
   are disabled, as no bigger data type can be used to do such tests. I
   simply test those data types using numbers slightly larger and smaller
   than the 32-bit integer min and max.

5. Use C defined macros to shorted lines of codes for different data types.
   This applies for all APIs.

6. Remove ncmpi_type. Just use nc_type.

7. Break ncx.c into files. One for each variable data type in file.
   getputn_schar.c, getputn_uchar.c,  getputn_short.c, getputn_int.c,
   getputn_float.c, getputn_double.c, getputn_ushort.c,
   getputn_uint.c,  getputn_int64.c,  getputn_uint64.c

commit message:
Prior to this commit, PnetCDF wraps each MPI read/write call in put/get APIs with two MPI_File_set_view(). One is before the MPI read/write call to take advantage of MPI's fileview feature for accessing non-contiguous file locations. The other is after the MPI read/write call to make the whole file visible, as the root process may write to file header later in the data mode and it alone cannot make a call to MPI_File_set_view() because the function is collective.

In this commit, the second MPI_File_set_view() has been removed. The root process's fileview is changed to always keep the whole file header visible. Saving a collective call to MPI_File_set_view() is expected to improve some performance.

commit message:
Check availability individual large count MPI functions

PnetCDF uses the following MPI datatype construction functions for large
requests.
    MPI_Type_create_subarray_c
    MPI_Type_contiguous_c
    MPI_Type_create_hvector_c
    MPI_Type_create_struct_c
    MPI_Type_create_hindexed_c
    MPI_Type_vector_c
    MPI_Pack_c
    MPI_Unpack_c
    MPI_Type_get_true_extent_x
    MPI_Type_size_x
If all are available, then define HAVE_MPI_LARGE_COUNT and proceed with
constructing large datatypes for fileview and user buffer. Checking
MPI_VERSION against 3 is not sufficient, as some MPI (e.g. OpenMPI
5.0.2) does not support MPI_XXX_c functions.

PR checks whether MPI Fortran compilers recognize this command-line
option and, if yes, adds it automatically to FFLAGS and FCFLAGS.

commit message:
1. After some thought, it makes little sense to keep varn, varns, and varnm,
   because varn is for multiple entire array accesses, varns is a subset of
   varna, and varnm is a subset of the flexible API. Hence, I decide to just
   invent get/put_varn_<type> APIs. For example,

   int ncmpi_put_varn_float(int                ncid,
                            int                varid,
                            int                num,
                            MPI_Offset* const  starts[],
                            MPI_Offset* const  counts[],
                            const float       *buf);

   This API allows writing 'num' subarrays of a variable.
   starts is a 2D array of size num x ndims, where ndims is the number of
   dimensions of the netCDF variable. Similarly, counts is also a 2D
   array of size num x ndims. Note that counts can be NULL, in which case
   is equivalent to counts being all 1s.

   Limitation: starts[*] must be in monotonically nondecreasing order with
               respective to the array indices. If the rule is violated,
               PnetCDF returns error code NC_NC_EVARNMONO.

2. The old implementation of varn APIs are kept in case we change mind,
   but it is not compiled. It is also renamed to varx.

commit message:
New benchmark programs that write multiple variables

* benchmarks/C/pnetcdf_put_vara.c
  + This program writes a series of 3D variables with 2D block-block
    partitioning pattern. Each variable is a record variable. The number of
    variables, variable size, number of time records, and the NetCDF file
    format can be customized through command-line options. In addition, option
    '-i', if set, PnetCDF nonblocking APIs will be used to write to the file.
* benchmarks/C/netcdf_put_vara.c
  + This sequential NetCDF-C program writes a series of 3D variables.  Each
    variable is a record variable. The number of variables, variable size,
    number of time records, and the NetCDF file format can be customized
    through command-line options.
  + This program and `C/pnetcdf_put_vara.c` can be used to compare the
    performance of NetCDF and PnetCDF when running sequentially, i.e. one
    process.

compatiblity fix for pnetcdf and netcdf4:

This way-overdue compatibilty fix was suggested by Ed Hartnett
<ed@unidata.ucar.edu>:  pnetcdf and netcdf share some of the same definitions.
When they differ (pnetcdf uses an enum, or netcdf has changed the
MAX_ATTR_LEN), programs including netcdf.h and pnetcdf.h will either fail to
compile or throw a warning.  So, we wrap pnetcdf defines in a _NETCDF_ block.

commit message:
The original design of nonblocking I/O is to concatenate the fileviews of individual nonblocking requests and serve them with a single MPI-IO call.  However, because MPI-IO requires the file displacements of the flattened fileview be monotonically nondecreasing, we divide the nonblocking requests into groups such that each group abides by the fileview requirement. Then, each group is carried out by a separate MPI-IO call. Performance can be poor if there are too many groups.

This revision fixes this problem by flattening all fileviews into offset-length pairs and merging all the pairs, so that the nonblocking requests can be carried out by a single MPI-IO call. Performance is expected to be improved as the number of MPI-IO calls is reduced to one.

However, be warned about the additional memory requirement. The additional memory needed for flatterning the fileviews might be more than the I/O data itself. For example, each offset-length pair represents only a 4-byte integer and the C struct for the offset-length pair takes 3*sizeof(MPI_Offset)=24 bytes.

following statement. "The second method involves providing the 'DESTDIR'
variable. For example, 'make install DESTDIR=/alternate/directory' will
prepend '/alternate/directory' before all installation names. The approach of
'DESTDIR' overrides is not required by the GNU Coding Standards, and does not
work on platforms that have drive letters. On the other hand, it does better
at avoiding recompilation issues, and works well even when some directory
options were not specified in terms of '${prefix}' at configure time."

commit message:
This commit is the first cut of supporting thread safety.
A pthread mutex is added in the following two files to protect global variables
and thread unsafe subroutine calls.
1. There are 3 global variables defined in src/dispatchers/file.c that need to
   be protected by mutex:
       static PNC *pnc_filelist[NC_MAX_NFILES];
       static int  pnc_numfiles;
       static int  ncmpi_default_create_format;
2. The binary tree used by tfind()/tsearch()/tdelete() cannot be updated safely
   in the multi-threading environment. Thus, calling these subroutines is
   protected by a mutex.

A test C program test/testcase/tst_pthread.c and an example C program
examples/C/pthread.c are added to test the one-file-per-thread I/O operations.

Note that this commit was only tested with the one-file-per-thread case. More
test cases will be added later.

commit message:
This revision has a bunch of changes.
They are mainly for preparing the future merge of independent and collective modes. The most noticable is the resetting the fileview every time a get/put is complete. In addition, creating filetype is avoided when a get/put request is contiguous in file. In this case, MPI-IO functions with explicit offset are used.

---- FILE: src/lib/header.c ----
hdr_fetch(): remove the call to MPI_File_set_view because the entire file is already visible. In addition, since MPI_File_read_at() is used, which does not change the file pointer, there is no need to reset fileview after MPI_File_read_at().

---- FILE: src/lib/mpincio.c ----
1. remove all unnecessary info objects passed in MPI_File_set_view.
2. ncmpiio_create() add a check for file existence by process 0 only,
   so MPI_File_set_size may be avoided.
3. ncmpiio_move(), change MPI independent I/O to collective. Also
   remove MPI_file_set_view, as they are not necessary.

---- FILE: src/lib/mpinetcdf.c ----
1. Add a new function in_swap() for in-place Endianness byte swap. htonl() and htons() are used to speedup the 2-byte and 4-byte swap operation.
2. Add a new function get_offset() that returns the starting file offset of a put/get request.
3. Add a new function is_request_contiguous() to check whether a put/get requst is contiguous in file.
4. Change all MPI_File_set_view() calls to use MPI_INFO_NULL, except for the ones in ncmpi_open() and ncmpi_create(). This avoids repeatedly passing the same MPI info object.
5. Change the code segments of updating the number of records in NC object in all ncmpi_put_xxx_all functions. When NC_doNsync(ncp) is true, ncp->numrecs is synchronized among all processes. Since ncmpii_write_numrecs() is a collective call, ncp->numrecs must agree among all processes.
6. Remove set_var1_fileview(), because accessing one variable element need not set fileview. The MPI-IO functions used to get/put the variable element are changed to the ones with explicit file offset.
7. In set_vara_fileview(), check if the request is contiguous in file. If yes, there is no need to create a fileype. Instead, a call to MPI_File_set_view() with explict file offset and MPI_BYTE filetype is used.

---- FILE: src/lib/nc.c ----
1. ncmpii_write_numrecs(): since this function is collective (only called by the pnetcdf collective APIs in mpinetcdf.c) clean up some independent operation residue.
2. Note that pnetcdf independent APIs do not call ncmpii_write_numrecs(), so the number of records may be inconsistent among processes !
3. write_NC(): MPI independent write is replaced with collective write. However, all processes write zero bytes except process 0. So, only process 0's header gets written to the file. Note that the header consistency check has already been done prior to this point.
4. ncmpii_read_numrecs(): remove MPI_File_set_view() as the fileview is always kept entire file visible and the file pointer to offset zero.

Create 4 new command-line define macros: NETCDF4_INC, NETCDF4_LDFLAGS,
NETCDF4_LIBS, and NETCDF4_PACKAGE. NETCDF4_INC is only needed when
NetCDF4 header files are needed, such as in src/dispatchers and
src/drivers/nc4io to resolve constants and APIs defines/declared
in NetCDF header files. NETCDF4_LDFLAGS and NETCDF4_LIBS are only
needed at linking time to produce executables, such as utility
programs, test and example programs. They are not needed when
building libraries. NETCDF4_PACKAGE is the name of package, to be
used in src/packaging/pnetcdf.pc.in.

commit message:
In CDF-2 format spec, NON_NEG is defined as <non-negative INT> and INT is a 32-bit signed integer. NetCDF interprets this to make NON_NEG an unsigned 32-bit integer and hence its range is from 0 to UINT_MAX (4294967295). This is one of the reasons netCDF uses arguments of type size_t (unsigned) in most of its APIs. For example, the maximal dimension for a CDF-2 file is 4294967295-3 (3 handles rounded-up size).

To conform with netCDF, in this PnetCDF revision, I made changes to treat NON_NEG as an unsigned 32/64-bit integer. Because the MPI_Offset integer arguments used in PnetCDF APIs are signed 64-bit integers, these arguments are now type-casted to/from NON_NEG, i.e. unsigned 32 or 64-bit integer for CDF-2 or CDF-5 format, respectively.

Maybe we should start thinking about replacing MPI_Offset with size_t (an unsigned 64-bit integer on 64-bit machines), like netCDF APIs. Perhaps this change makes an easier integration of PnetCDF to netCDF.

commit message:
Change the use of MPI_File_sync() in a more consistent way: MPI_File_sync() will only be called when the file is opened/created with NC_SHARE mode.

This provides users an option for more strict file consistency (by using NC_SHARE/NF_SHARE mode when open/create a file).

Based on the open mode, the use of MPI_File_sync() has been changed to the folllowings.

1) When NC_SHARE mode is not used, header in memory will kept sync-ed across all processes. No MPI_File_sync() will be called. Header will be written to the file at ncmpi_enddef() and ncmpi_close(), but not file sync. MPI_File_sync() will only be called in ncmpi_begin_indep_data(), ncmpi_end_indep_data() and ncmpi_sync().

2) When NC_SHARE mode is used, MPI_File_sync() will be called implicitly in the following APIs: a) ncmpi_enddef(); b) all collective put APIs that increase the number of records; c) all (collective) attribute APIs that change attributes (legally); and d) ncmpi_close().

programs that use those constants to check whether the deprecated
constants are "useable", i.e. not defined to error messages.

author: Wei-keng Liao <wkliao@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
This commit revises the implementation of nonblocking APIs.  Prior to this
revision, the pending nonblocking requests are stored in put_list and get_list
arrays, for both lead and non-lead requests.  Lead requests are the requests
called from nonblocking APIs and non-lead requests are the sub-requests derived
from the leads, such as individual record requests from a single iput_vara API
call or individual requests from a single varn API call.  This revision
separates the pending requests into put_lead_list and put_list, where
put_lead_list contains only lead requests and put_list contains only non-lead
requests. Same for the get lists. Non-lead lists are used to construct filetype
and buftypes. They can be freed before calling MPI_File_write or MPI_File_read,
and hence save memory space before entering MPI-IO.  The lead lists are used to
free temporarily allocated memory, byte-swap, type-conversion, or
buffer-unpacking after MPI-IO.  This approach reduces the memory footprint for
nonblocking APIs that generate a large number of non-lead requests, such as
varn APIs.

commit message:
I am facing a problem that MPI-IO does not return error codes consistently. For example, when file open mode (access mode) is not the same among all processes, MPI should return MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME. But some MPI versions (older MPICH and OpenMPI) return MPI_ERR_AMODE instead.
PnetCDF relies on MPI error classes to produce corresponding error codes in PnetCDF. For instance, starting from PnetCDF 1.4.0, MPI_ERR_AMODE is translated to NC_EMULTIDEFINE_OMODE. However, MPI_ERR_AMODE does not just mean inconsistent file access mode, and hence this needs to change.
In this commit, I create a new error code NC_EMULTIDEFINE_FNC_ARGS corresponding to MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME. If PnetCDF omode or cmode is inconsistent, then it reports NC_EMULTIDEFINE_FNC_ARGS if MPI-IO can return MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME correctly. Otherwise, if MPI-IO retruns MPI_ERR_AMODE, then we still translate it to NC_EMULTIDEFINE_OMODE, as in PnetCDF there is no other way to cause MPI_ERR_AMODE.

commit message:
This revision has a bunch of changes.
They are mainly for preparing the future merge of independent and collective modes. The most noticable is the resetting the fileview every time a get/put is complete. In addition, creating filetype is avoided when a get/put request is contiguous in file. In this case, MPI-IO functions with explicit offset are used.

---- FILE: src/lib/header.c ----
hdr_fetch(): remove the call to MPI_File_set_view because the entire file is already visible. In addition, since MPI_File_read_at() is used, which does not change the file pointer, there is no need to reset fileview after MPI_File_read_at().

---- FILE: src/lib/mpincio.c ----
1. remove all unnecessary info objects passed in MPI_File_set_view.
2. ncmpiio_create() add a check for file existence by process 0 only,
   so MPI_File_set_size may be avoided.
3. ncmpiio_move(), change MPI independent I/O to collective. Also
   remove MPI_file_set_view, as they are not necessary.

---- FILE: src/lib/mpinetcdf.c ----
1. Add a new function in_swap() for in-place Endianness byte swap. htonl() and htons() are used to speedup the 2-byte and 4-byte swap operation.
2. Add a new function get_offset() that returns the starting file offset of a put/get request.
3. Add a new function is_request_contiguous() to check whether a put/get requst is contiguous in file.
4. Change all MPI_File_set_view() calls to use MPI_INFO_NULL, except for the ones in ncmpi_open() and ncmpi_create(). This avoids repeatedly passing the same MPI info object.
5. Change the code segments of updating the number of records in NC object in all ncmpi_put_xxx_all functions. When NC_doNsync(ncp) is true, ncp->numrecs is synchronized among all processes. Since ncmpii_write_numrecs() is a collective call, ncp->numrecs must agree among all processes.
6. Remove set_var1_fileview(), because accessing one variable element need not set fileview. The MPI-IO functions used to get/put the variable element are changed to the ones with explicit file offset.
7. In set_vara_fileview(), check if the request is contiguous in file. If yes, there is no need to create a fileype. Instead, a call to MPI_File_set_view() with explict file offset and MPI_BYTE filetype is used.

---- FILE: src/lib/nc.c ----
1. ncmpii_write_numrecs(): since this function is collective (only called by the pnetcdf collective APIs in mpinetcdf.c) clean up some independent operation residue.
2. Note that pnetcdf independent APIs do not call ncmpii_write_numrecs(), so the number of records may be inconsistent among processes !
3. write_NC(): MPI independent write is replaced with collective write. However, all processes write zero bytes except process 0. So, only process 0's header gets written to the file. Note that the header consistency check has already been done prior to this point.
4. ncmpii_read_numrecs(): remove MPI_File_set_view() as the fileview is always kept entire file visible and the file pointer to offset zero.

commit message:
The original design of nonblocking I/O is to concatenate the fileviews of individual nonblocking requests and serve them with a single MPI-IO call.  However, because MPI-IO requires the file displacements of the flattened fileview be monotonically nondecreasing, we divide the nonblocking requests into groups such that each group abides by the fileview requirement. Then, each group is carried out by a separate MPI-IO call. Performance can be poor if there are too many groups.

This revision fixes this problem by flattening all fileviews into offset-length pairs and merging all the pairs, so that the nonblocking requests can be carried out by a single MPI-IO call. Performance is expected to be improved as the number of MPI-IO calls is reduced to one.

However, be warned about the additional memory requirement. The additional memory needed for flatterning the fileviews might be more than the I/O data itself. For example, each offset-length pair represents only a 4-byte integer and the C struct for the offset-length pair takes 3*sizeof(MPI_Offset)=24 bytes.

commit message:
As file header is read in chunks of size 256KB each, the actual read
amount can be smaller than the chunk size for small files. Because the
whole chunk is broadcasted to all processes, regardless the actual
read amount, the read buffer will contain uninitialized values which
may be complained by valgrind. This happens when running E3SM-IO
benchmark F case where valgrind complains uninitialized values all
over place in a collective write call.

commit message:
This major revision contains the followings.

1) src/lib/mpinetcdf.c is now split into several files, based on the APIs' names.

2) codes restructured for blocking APIs. All blocking put and get APIs are now pointing to the combined function ncmpii_getput_vars().

3) revise nonblocking APIs. Similar to blocking APIs, all get put APIs are pointing to ncmpii_igetput_varm().

4) regulate nonblocking APIs sematics. All nonblocking APIs can now be called either in independent or collective data mode. There are only two wait calls are implemented: ncmpi_wait() must be called in independent mode and ncmpi_wait_all() must be called in collective mode.

5) nonblocking Fortran APIs are regenerated.

6) test codes for nonblocking APIs are added. See test/nc_test and test/nf_test.

7) User manual is updated to reflect the changes in 4).

commit message:
Add AX_COMPILER_VENDOR and MPI_COMPILER_BASE

AX_COMPILER_VENDOR returns the vendor of the C, C++ or Fortran compiler in
ax_cv_c_compiler_vendor, ax_cv_cxx_compiler_vendor, ax_cv_fc_compiler_vendor.
See https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf-archive/ax_compiler_vendor.html

MPI_COMPILER_BASE returns the base compiler command used in MPI compiler
wrapper in ac_cv_mpi_compiler_base_MPICC, ac_cv_mpi_compiler_base_MPICXX,
ac_cv_mpi_compiler_base_MPIF90, such as /usr/bin/gcc, /usr/bin/g++,
/usr/bin/gfortran

commit message:
Bugs fixed to pass most tests in "nc_test":

1.
I didn't include "BYTE" datatype support in the parallel implementation, while
the nc_test DOES require this and expect type-related errors in the test. Now,
I've added this kind of support.

2.
Some of the error codes are not catched in ncmpi, while nc_test DOES expect the correct codes in time of specific errors. I've fixed them.

3.
nc_test is tightly connected with the authors' serial netCDF implementation
code. Most FAILURE in our test is due to "incorrect" test.nc file which is
generated by nc_test itself. In serial nc_test, the authors assume if some
error (e.g. datatype range error) happens, the (overflowed) data is still
written into file, while in the parallel netCDF implementation, I chose to
abort with the error code returned. I've changed it to follow the same rule
to satisfy nc_test.

4. [FATAL]
The type conversion between int and float is incorrect in ncmpi implementation. I've fixed it.

5.
In time of multi-errors, the serial netcdf check these errors in a different
sequential order than ncmpi implementation, while nc_test assumes and expects
the former. I've changed it to follow the same order to satisfy nc_test.

6.
Some special-case errors were not detected and make nc_test crash, e.g.
MPI_Type_create_subarray crashes when 0-subsize is specified.

commit message:
This commit revises the implementation of nonblocking APIs.  Prior to this
revision, the pending nonblocking requests are stored in put_list and get_list
arrays, for both lead and non-lead requests.  Lead requests are the requests
called from nonblocking APIs and non-lead requests are the sub-requests derived
from the leads, such as individual record requests from a single iput_vara API
call or individual requests from a single varn API call.  This revision
separates the pending requests into put_lead_list and put_list, where
put_lead_list contains only lead requests and put_list contains only non-lead
requests. Same for the get lists. Non-lead lists are used to construct filetype
and buftypes. They can be freed before calling MPI_File_write or MPI_File_read,
and hence save memory space before entering MPI-IO.  The lead lists are used to
free temporarily allocated memory, byte-swap, type-conversion, or
buffer-unpacking after MPI-IO.  This approach reduces the memory footprint for
nonblocking APIs that generate a large number of non-lead requests, such as
varn APIs.

commit message:
bug fix for really big short and uchar variables from the unidata folks.  

http://www.unidata.ucar.edu/software/netcdf/docs/known_problems.html#large_vars_362 

Bugs in support for variables larger than 4 GiB

As first reported by Mario Emmenlauer, there is a bug in netCDF-3.6.2 (and
earlier versions) in the code for creating byte and short type variables
greater than 4 GiB in size. This problem resulted in an assertion violation or
arithmetic exception that would have caused a program to halt, rather than
writing bad data or corrupting existing data.

A fix is available as a patch to the file libsrc/var.c in the netcdf-3.6.2
distribution. The bug is also fixed in the latest netCDF-3 snapshot release.

   1. On 32-bit platforms (with size_t an unsigned 32-bit type):
      * For a short variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**31 (that's 2147483648), the
	following assertion violation occurs

            Assertion failed: remaining > 0, file putget.c, line 347

      * For any type of variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting
	the record dimension, if any) is exactly 2**32 (that's 4294967296) or
	any multiple of 2**32, a divide by zero occurs

            Arithmetic Exception(coredump)

   2. On 64-bit platforms (with size_t an unsigned 64-bit type):
      * For a byte variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**32, an assertion violation
        occurs

            Assertion failed: *ulp <= X_SIZE_MAX, file ncx.c, line 1810

      * For a short variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**31, the same assertion
        violation occurs

            Assertion failed: *ulp <= X_SIZE_MAX, file ncx.c, line 1810

commit message:
Prior to this commit, PnetCDF wraps each MPI read/write call in put/get APIs with two MPI_File_set_view(). One is before the MPI read/write call to take advantage of MPI's fileview feature for accessing non-contiguous file locations. The other is after the MPI read/write call to make the whole file visible, as the root process may write to file header later in the data mode and it alone cannot make a call to MPI_File_set_view() because the function is collective.

In this commit, the second MPI_File_set_view() has been removed. The root process's fileview is changed to always keep the whole file header visible. Saving a collective call to MPI_File_set_view() is expected to improve some performance.

commit message:
Dimension size limit should be INT_MAX

According to NetCDF CDF 1 and 2 file format specification, the maximal
dimension size should be INT_MAX, i.e. 2^31-1, <non-negative INT>.

NetCDF file format specification:
  netcdf_file  = header data
  header       = magic numrecs dim_list gatt_list var_list
  dim_list     = ABSENT | NC_DIMENSION nelems [dim ...]
  dim          = name dim_length
  dim_length   = NON_NEG
  NON_NEG      = <non-negative INT>
  INT          = <32-bit signed integer, Bigendian, two's complement>

Note for variable size, the maximal is
  2^31-3  for CDF-1
  2^32-3  for CDF-2
  2^63-3  for CDF-5
Variable size is calculated internally in PnetCDF. Therefor, the
variable size is limited to the space available in bytes. -3 is
due to the 4-byte upward alignment.
Also, note vsize defined in the file header format is not used.

commit message:
Reuse length of name string, instead of calling strlen

In NetCDF format spec, object `name` consists of two parts: the number
of characters and the character string itself, i.e.
```
    name = nelems namestring
```
where `nelems` is the length of `namestring`.
This commit reuses `nelems` if it is previously calculated or already
available in the file header, so to avoid calls to `strlen()`.

commit message:
This revision strengthens data consistency for the number of records.

1. In collective data mode, when a record variable is written (from a call to a put API), the number of records will be synchronized among all processes' memory. If NC_SHARE is set, the number will be written to the file. In order to achieve this, an MPI_Allreduce() is added at the end of put APIs. Only process of rank 0 writes to the file header.

2. In independent data mode, the number of records stored in memory may be inconsistent among processes. There is no automatic solution to synchronized it without a collective operation, not even if by writing the number of records to the file. A race condition can occur if making multiple processes write to file concurrently, as this write requires a) read numrecs; b) check if new numrecs is larger; c) if larger, write/update the new numrecs to file header.

3. A new API, ncmpi_sync_numrecs(ncid), is added. Users are encouraged to call it to synchronized the number of records if in independent data mode.

4. For nonblocking APIs and ncmpi_wait_all() is called, the synchronization for numrecs is performed, as some processes might be writing to record variables and some not.

Others changes not related to consistency:

1. delay temporary buffer allocation (lbuf and cbuf) for read operation after MPI read.

2. NCcoordck() now checks if it is called from a get or put API, rather than checking NC_readonly(ncp) for read-only file.

commit message:
This revision strengthens data consistency for the number of records.

1. In collective data mode, when a record variable is written (from a call to a put API), the number of records will be synchronized among all processes' memory. If NC_SHARE is set, the number will be written to the file. In order to achieve this, an MPI_Allreduce() is added at the end of put APIs. Only process of rank 0 writes to the file header.

2. In independent data mode, the number of records stored in memory may be inconsistent among processes. There is no automatic solution to synchronized it without a collective operation, not even if by writing the number of records to the file. A race condition can occur if making multiple processes write to file concurrently, as this write requires a) read numrecs; b) check if new numrecs is larger; c) if larger, write/update the new numrecs to file header.

3. A new API, ncmpi_sync_numrecs(ncid), is added. Users are encouraged to call it to synchronized the number of records if in independent data mode.

4. For nonblocking APIs and ncmpi_wait_all() is called, the synchronization for numrecs is performed, as some processes might be writing to record variables and some not.

Others changes not related to consistency:

1. delay temporary buffer allocation (lbuf and cbuf) for read operation after MPI read.

2. NCcoordck() now checks if it is called from a get or put API, rather than checking NC_readonly(ncp) for read-only file.

commit message:
This major revision contains the followings.

1) src/lib/mpinetcdf.c is now split into several files, based on the APIs' names.

2) codes restructured for blocking APIs. All blocking put and get APIs are now pointing to the combined function ncmpii_getput_vars().

3) revise nonblocking APIs. Similar to blocking APIs, all get put APIs are pointing to ncmpii_igetput_varm().

4) regulate nonblocking APIs sematics. All nonblocking APIs can now be called either in independent or collective data mode. There are only two wait calls are implemented: ncmpi_wait() must be called in independent mode and ncmpi_wait_all() must be called in collective mode.

5) nonblocking Fortran APIs are regenerated.

6) test codes for nonblocking APIs are added. See test/nc_test and test/nf_test.

7) User manual is updated to reflect the changes in 4).

commit message:
This revision is mainly to support the new data types introduced in CDF-5
specification: UBYTE, USHORT, UINT, INT64, and UINT64

1. Support the following CDF-5 data types for C APIs:
   unsigned short, unsigned int, 64-bit integer (int64), unsigned int64
   New APIs: ncmpi_put_vara_ushort(), ncmpi_put_vara_uint(),
             ncmpi_put_vara_longlong(), and ncmpi_put_vara_ulonglong(), etc.

2. Support the following CDF-5 data types for Fortran APIs:
   64-bit integer (int8)
   New APIs: nfmpi_put_vara_int8(), etc.

3. The new APIs follow the looks of netCDF4.

4. Extend test program, nc_test and nf_test, to test the new data types.
   Note that for data types int64 and uint64, test for out-of-bound values
   are disabled, as no bigger data type can be used to do such tests. I
   simply test those data types using numbers slightly larger and smaller
   than the 32-bit integer min and max.

5. Use C defined macros to shorted lines of codes for different data types.
   This applies for all APIs.

6. Remove ncmpi_type. Just use nc_type.

7. Break ncx.c into files. One for each variable data type in file.
   getputn_schar.c, getputn_uchar.c,  getputn_short.c, getputn_int.c,
   getputn_float.c, getputn_double.c, getputn_ushort.c,
   getputn_uint.c,  getputn_int64.c,  getputn_uint64.c

commit message:
1. After some thought, it makes little sense to keep varn, varns, and varnm,
   because varn is for multiple entire array accesses, varns is a subset of
   varna, and varnm is a subset of the flexible API. Hence, I decide to just
   invent get/put_varn_<type> APIs. For example,

   int ncmpi_put_varn_float(int                ncid,
                            int                varid,
                            int                num,
                            MPI_Offset* const  starts[],
                            MPI_Offset* const  counts[],
                            const float       *buf);

   This API allows writing 'num' subarrays of a variable.
   starts is a 2D array of size num x ndims, where ndims is the number of
   dimensions of the netCDF variable. Similarly, counts is also a 2D
   array of size num x ndims. Note that counts can be NULL, in which case
   is equivalent to counts being all 1s.

   Limitation: starts[*] must be in monotonically nondecreasing order with
               respective to the array indices. If the rule is violated,
               PnetCDF returns error code NC_NC_EVARNMONO.

2. The old implementation of varn APIs are kept in case we change mind,
   but it is not compiled. It is also renamed to varx.

commit message:
I/O hint precedences

* 1st priority: hints set in the environment variable `PNETCDF_HINTS`,
  e.g. `PNETCDF_HINTS="nc_var_align_size=1048576"`
* 2nd priority: hints set in the MPI info objects passed into calls to
  `ncmpi_create()` and `ncmpi_open()`, e.g.
  `MPI_Info_set("nc_var_align_size", "1048576");`
* 3rd priority: hints passed from arguments of `ncmpi__enddef()`, e.g.
  `ncmpi__enddef(..., v_align=1048576,...)`

When both hints `nc_var_align_size` and `nc_header_align_size` are set
in the environment variable `PNETCDF_HINTS` or MPI info object, only
`nc_var_align_size` will take effect.

When there is no fix-sized variables defined, argument `v_minfree` is
ignored. In this case, users should set `h_minfree`, if extra header
space is desired.

When there is no fix-sized variables defined and `v_align` is not set,
hint `r_align`, if set, will be used as `v_align` to align the header
extent.

commit message:
I am facing a problem that MPI-IO does not return error codes consistently. For example, when file open mode (access mode) is not the same among all processes, MPI should return MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME. But some MPI versions (older MPICH and OpenMPI) return MPI_ERR_AMODE instead.
PnetCDF relies on MPI error classes to produce corresponding error codes in PnetCDF. For instance, starting from PnetCDF 1.4.0, MPI_ERR_AMODE is translated to NC_EMULTIDEFINE_OMODE. However, MPI_ERR_AMODE does not just mean inconsistent file access mode, and hence this needs to change.
In this commit, I create a new error code NC_EMULTIDEFINE_FNC_ARGS corresponding to MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME. If PnetCDF omode or cmode is inconsistent, then it reports NC_EMULTIDEFINE_FNC_ARGS if MPI-IO can return MPI_ERR_NOT_SAME correctly. Otherwise, if MPI-IO retruns MPI_ERR_AMODE, then we still translate it to NC_EMULTIDEFINE_OMODE, as in PnetCDF there is no other way to cause MPI_ERR_AMODE.

commit message:
Stop using file striping size to automatically set header extent

Automatically set the size of file header extent using the file striping
size obtained from MPI-IO hint striping_unit may yield an unexpectedly
large file header extent and cause movement of data sections if new
metadata is added when the program re-enter the define mode. With this
commit, file striping size will no longer be used to set the file header
alignment size. However, users can still set nc_header_align_size in
PNETCDF_HINTS environment variable or v_align in ncmpi__enddef() to
customize the size of header extent.

checks whether the supplied MPI C compiler is a wrapper of a C++ compiler

PnetCDF configuration will be aborted. This check is enforced because
using such an MPI C compiler will cause problem for linking Fortran, C
and C++ programs, with an error message similar to this:
 conftestf.o: In function `MAIN_': conftestf.f:4: undefined reference to `sub_'

author: wkliao <wkliao@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Performance tuning: for nonblocking requests of more than one record

The original design to keep the pending list of nonblocking requests
sorted based on the variable's begin offsets is to avoid an expensive
sorting at ncmpi_wait_all. However, the design only assumes all pending
requests of record variables are for the same record, and thus the
sorting uses the beginnings of the record variables (first records).
This design was reasonable, as usually the application would flush all
pending requests to one record before posting requests to the next
record. Therefore, when nonblocking requests consist of multiple
records, inserting the new requests of next record into the pending list
becomes expensive. This commit improves the design by using the
beginnings of variable's individual records.

commit message:
Revisit ncmpii_create() for handling NC_CLOBBER and NC_NOCLOBBER modes.

When NC_CLOBBER mode is used, we abandon the possibility to call MPI_File_set_size because this call is expensive. Instead, we delete the file. If unlink() is available, we use it and ignore error code ENOENT. If unlink() is not available, we use MPI_File_delete and ignore error class MPI_ERR_NO_SUCH_FILE.

However, ROMIO as in today does not correctly return MPI_ERR_NO_SUCH_FILE on many file systems. Hence, user may get NC_EOFILE error instead.

For NC_NOCLOBBER, netCDF requires to return error NC_EEXIST if the file exists. When access() is not available, we use MPI_MODE_EXCL mode in MPI_File_open in expecting error class MPI_ERR_FILE_EXISTS returned if the file exists. Again, ROMIO as in today does not correctly return MPI_ERR_FILE_EXISTS. This makes returnning NC_EEXIST as required by netCDF difficult.

A temporary solution is added that lets rank 0 braodcast errno and then check its value against EEXIST. This is still not perfect. Hope ROMIO soon will be fixed on returning erro classes.

Note when both access() and unlink() are available, the above problem does not appear, as rank 0 broadcasts file_exist or error code at the end.

commit message:
Fix the program hanging problem caused by CHECK_MPI_ERROR which returns an error in the middle of a function. In this case, any collective operation following CHECK_MPI_ERROR may not be reachable to those processes with MPI error code returned. Because MPI does not require collective operations return the same error code for all processes, the processes obtaining MPI_SUCCESS will continue to the next MPI collective operations, waiting indefinitely for those with error code and hence casue the program to hang.

This fix also makes the MPI errors less priorty than the NC errors, i.e. if both errors occur, only the NC error will be returned.

commit message:
I/O hint precedences

* 1st priority: hints set in the environment variable `PNETCDF_HINTS`,
  e.g. `PNETCDF_HINTS="nc_var_align_size=1048576"`
* 2nd priority: hints set in the MPI info objects passed into calls to
  `ncmpi_create()` and `ncmpi_open()`, e.g.
  `MPI_Info_set("nc_var_align_size", "1048576");`
* 3rd priority: hints passed from arguments of `ncmpi__enddef()`, e.g.
  `ncmpi__enddef(..., v_align=1048576,...)`

When both hints `nc_var_align_size` and `nc_header_align_size` are set
in the environment variable `PNETCDF_HINTS` or MPI info object, only
`nc_var_align_size` will take effect.

When there is no fix-sized variables defined, argument `v_minfree` is
ignored. In this case, users should set `h_minfree`, if extra header
space is desired.

When there is no fix-sized variables defined and `v_align` is not set,
hint `r_align`, if set, will be used as `v_align` to align the header
extent.

commit message:
call lstat to check if a file is a regular file

* When using NC_CLOBBER when calling ncmpi_create, the file must be truncated
  to of zero size. This was implemented using truncate() or MPI_File_open() +
  MPI_File_set_size(), which can be expensive on HPC machines.
* This commit calls lstat() to check if the file to be clobbered is a regular
  file. If yes, call unlink() or MPI_File_delete(), which should be faster then
  truncate() or MPI_File_set_size().
* However, the best performance is for applications to delete/truncate the file
  before run.

author: Rob Latham <rlatham@gmail.com>
commit message:
bugfix from serial netcdf:

The bug occurs following this sequence of steps:

   1. A large netCDF file is created using the new 64-bit offset format variant
      (also known as the version 2 format) and the file is closed.

   2. Later the file is opened for writing, followed by either of the following
      operations:
	  * enter define mode (calling nc_redef(), nf_redef(), or nf90_redef(),
	    in C, Fortran-77, or Fortran-90 interface, for example) to add a
	    new dimension, variable, or attribute; or

	  * write a new value for an existing attribute (either a global or a
	    variable-specific attribute).

Under these conditions, after you leave define mode or close the file, the file
header is written out in the "classic" (version 1) netCDF format, chopping the
leading bits off any variable offsets that were large enough to require more
than 32 bits

commit message:
add implementation to ignore file layout order of variables

NetCDF file format specification contains a comment below about the
file space locations of non-record variables in the data section:

   non_recs = [vardata ...] // The data for all non-record variables,
                            // stored contiguously for each variable, in
                            // the same order the variables occur in the
                            // header.

The similar comment does not appear for record variables.

This requirement is actually not necessary, as each variable has a
'begin' entity in the header pointing to the starting file location
storing its data. Removing this requirement has an advantage when
file header needs to expand. It allows to move only the first few
variables large enough for the required additional header space to
locations with high file offsets, effectively reducing the expensive
data movement. Note we cannot change the variable order already in the
file header, as applications may already hold variable IDs that point to
the variable array indices in the header.

However, this relaxation may result in the earlier PnetCDF and NetCDF
versions complaining the file format error with NC_ENOTNC.

commit message:
bug fix for really big short and uchar variables from the unidata folks.  

http://www.unidata.ucar.edu/software/netcdf/docs/known_problems.html#large_vars_362 

Bugs in support for variables larger than 4 GiB

As first reported by Mario Emmenlauer, there is a bug in netCDF-3.6.2 (and
earlier versions) in the code for creating byte and short type variables
greater than 4 GiB in size. This problem resulted in an assertion violation or
arithmetic exception that would have caused a program to halt, rather than
writing bad data or corrupting existing data.

A fix is available as a patch to the file libsrc/var.c in the netcdf-3.6.2
distribution. The bug is also fixed in the latest netCDF-3 snapshot release.

   1. On 32-bit platforms (with size_t an unsigned 32-bit type):
      * For a short variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**31 (that's 2147483648), the
	following assertion violation occurs

            Assertion failed: remaining > 0, file putget.c, line 347

      * For any type of variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting
	the record dimension, if any) is exactly 2**32 (that's 4294967296) or
	any multiple of 2**32, a divide by zero occurs

            Arithmetic Exception(coredump)

   2. On 64-bit platforms (with size_t an unsigned 64-bit type):
      * For a byte variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**32, an assertion violation
        occurs

            Assertion failed: *ulp <= X_SIZE_MAX, file ncx.c, line 1810

      * For a short variable, if the product of dimensions (not counting the
	record dimension, if any) is greater than 2**31, the same assertion
        violation occurs

            Assertion failed: *ulp <= X_SIZE_MAX, file ncx.c, line 1810

commit message:
Fix the program hanging problem caused by CHECK_MPI_ERROR which returns an error in the middle of a function. In this case, any collective operation following CHECK_MPI_ERROR may not be reachable to those processes with MPI error code returned. Because MPI does not require collective operations return the same error code for all processes, the processes obtaining MPI_SUCCESS will continue to the next MPI collective operations, waiting indefinitely for those with error code and hence casue the program to hang.

This fix also makes the MPI errors less priorty than the NC errors, i.e. if both errors occur, only the NC error will be returned.

commit message:
= PnetCDF file header synchronization mechanism =

== Synchronize header data cached in memory ==

1. Changes to attributes, names of variables and dimensions
The following APIs can modify file header while being called in data mode. Note that these APIs can only modify existing attributes, rename variables or dimensions, given that the new attributes and names do not take more file space than the old ones. Otherwise, these APIs are prohibited in data mode.

    ncmpi_rename_dim(),
    ncmpi_rename_var(),
    ncmpi_copy_att(),
    ncmpi_rename_att(), and
    ncmpii_put_att_<type>()

The above semantics implemented in PnetCDF conform with the netCDF for the corresponding APIs. However, since PnetCDF is designed to handle parallel I/O to shared files, it must ensure data consistency for the file header that is cached in the memory of all MPI processes.  In order to do so, PnetCDF requires the above APIs to be called collectively and use the same argument values while in data mode.  PnetCDF does not automatically check the argument consistency, unless the program is in safe mode, i.e. the environment variable PNETCDF_SAFE_MODE is set to 1. Consistency checking requires one or more MPI collective communication operations, a cost some users may want to avoid.  Please note that the above consistency issue is about the file header data that is cached in the memory. For committing the head changes to the file, see below.

2. Changes to the number of records
At the end of collective put APIs that write record variables, PnetCDF synchronizes the number of records across all processes. This memory synchronization is enforced even if the program is not in the safe mode.  On the other hand for independent APIs, the number of records is not automatically synchronized, as memory synchronization requires MPI collective communication calls. Users are encouraged to call ncmpi_sync_numrecs() to explicitly synchronize the number of records. Note this new API is collective, but can be called in the independent data mode. Number of records is stored in the file header. For committing the number of records to the file, please see below.

== Commit header changes to file ==
In PnetCDF, only root process (rank 0) can write/read/modify the file header.  Thus, committing the changes to file header is done through the root. Before writing to file header, PnetCDF checks the consistency of header data cached in memory across MPI processes.  However, PnetCDF does not commit the header changes immediately to the file, unless the file is opened/created in NC_SHARE mode. If NC_SHARE is not set, the changes to the header data will be cached in memory and flushed to the file when calling ncmpi_close().

If you expect your PnetCDF program to be interrupted or exit in between a file open and close (due to returned error codes or system cash) and wish the file contains most up-to-date metadata (e.g. number of records), NC_SHARE mode should be used.

commit message:
Change the use of MPI_File_sync() in a more consistent way: MPI_File_sync() will only be called when the file is opened/created with NC_SHARE mode.

This provides users an option for more strict file consistency (by using NC_SHARE/NF_SHARE mode when open/create a file).

Based on the open mode, the use of MPI_File_sync() has been changed to the folllowings.

1) When NC_SHARE mode is not used, header in memory will kept sync-ed across all processes. No MPI_File_sync() will be called. Header will be written to the file at ncmpi_enddef() and ncmpi_close(), but not file sync. MPI_File_sync() will only be called in ncmpi_begin_indep_data(), ncmpi_end_indep_data() and ncmpi_sync().

2) When NC_SHARE mode is used, MPI_File_sync() will be called implicitly in the following APIs: a) ncmpi_enddef(); b) all collective put APIs that increase the number of records; c) all (collective) attribute APIs that change attributes (legally); and d) ncmpi_close().

commit message:
Create 4 new command-line define macros: NETCDF4_INC, NETCDF4_LDFLAGS,
NETCDF4_LIBS, and NETCDF4_PACKAGE. NETCDF4_INC is only needed when
NetCDF4 header files are needed, such as in src/dispatchers and
src/drivers/nc4io to resolve constants and APIs defines/declared
in NetCDF header files. NETCDF4_LDFLAGS and NETCDF4_LIBS are only
needed at linking time to produce executables, such as utility
programs, test and example programs. They are not needed when
building libraries. NETCDF4_PACKAGE is the name of package, to be
used in src/packaging/pnetcdf.pc.in.
