commit message:
Revisit ncmpii_create() for handling NC_CLOBBER and NC_NOCLOBBER modes.

When NC_CLOBBER mode is used, we abandon the possibility to call MPI_File_set_size because this call is expensive. Instead, we delete the file. If unlink() is available, we use it and ignore error code ENOENT. If unlink() is not available, we use MPI_File_delete and ignore error class MPI_ERR_NO_SUCH_FILE.

However, ROMIO as in today does not correctly return MPI_ERR_NO_SUCH_FILE on many file systems. Hence, user may get NC_EOFILE error instead.

For NC_NOCLOBBER, netCDF requires to return error NC_EEXIST if the file exists. When access() is not available, we use MPI_MODE_EXCL mode in MPI_File_open in expecting error class MPI_ERR_FILE_EXISTS returned if the file exists. Again, ROMIO as in today does not correctly return MPI_ERR_FILE_EXISTS. This makes returnning NC_EEXIST as required by netCDF difficult.

A temporary solution is added that lets rank 0 braodcast errno and then check its value against EEXIST. This is still not perfect. Hope ROMIO soon will be fixed on returning erro classes.

Note when both access() and unlink() are available, the above problem does not appear, as rank 0 broadcasts file_exist or error code at the end.

commit message:
In CDF-2 format spec, NON_NEG is defined as <non-negative INT> and INT is a 32-bit signed integer. NetCDF interprets this to make NON_NEG an unsigned 32-bit integer and hence its range is from 0 to UINT_MAX (4294967295). This is one of the reasons netCDF uses arguments of type size_t (unsigned) in most of its APIs. For example, the maximal dimension for a CDF-2 file is 4294967295-3 (3 handles rounded-up size).

To conform with netCDF, in this PnetCDF revision, I made changes to treat NON_NEG as an unsigned 32/64-bit integer. Because the MPI_Offset integer arguments used in PnetCDF APIs are signed 64-bit integers, these arguments are now type-casted to/from NON_NEG, i.e. unsigned 32 or 64-bit integer for CDF-2 or CDF-5 format, respectively.

Maybe we should start thinking about replacing MPI_Offset with size_t (an unsigned 64-bit integer on 64-bit machines), like netCDF APIs. Perhaps this change makes an easier integration of PnetCDF to netCDF.

author: Rob Latham <rlatham@gmail.com>
commit message:
bugfix from serial netcdf:

The bug occurs following this sequence of steps:

   1. A large netCDF file is created using the new 64-bit offset format variant
      (also known as the version 2 format) and the file is closed.

   2. Later the file is opened for writing, followed by either of the following
      operations:
	  * enter define mode (calling nc_redef(), nf_redef(), or nf90_redef(),
	    in C, Fortran-77, or Fortran-90 interface, for example) to add a
	    new dimension, variable, or attribute; or

	  * write a new value for an existing attribute (either a global or a
	    variable-specific attribute).

Under these conditions, after you leave define mode or close the file, the file
header is written out in the "classic" (version 1) netCDF format, chopping the
leading bits off any variable offsets that were large enough to require more
than 32 bits

Improve diffuse tensor velocity (#160)

This makes two changes:
* when computing the RHS with do_mom_diff==1, multiply U_new by rho_new
(rather than rho_old); i.e. use
rho^(n+1) * Unew = rho^(n+1) * [(rho^n U^n - dt U dot grad U +
...)/rho^(n+1)]
* pass a better initial guess for the solution to the tensor solver.
This can change results up to the tolerance of the viscous solve
(default relative tol = 1e-10)

author: Brian Friesen <bfriesen@lbl.gov>
commit message:
NS_util: move OpenMP user-defined reduction machinery outside namespace

If this UDR is defined inside the 'amrex' namespace, the Cray compiler
complains that it is incompletely defined. If it is moved outside the
namespace, then the compiler is happy.  Intel did not complain about this
either way.

I don't see anything in the OpenMP spec that says whether this is right or
wrong. The closest thing I could find is in section 2.16 of the OpenMP 4.5
spec, which says

  The declare reduction directive can also appear at points in the program at
  which a static data member could be declared. In this case, the visibility and
  accessibility of the declaration are the same as those of a static data member
  declared at the same point in the program.

I will submit this test case to Cray to find out if they think the compiler is
correct or if it is a compiler bug.

commit message:
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/code_cleanup' into development

Remove Fortran code, including the Fortran inputs file probin_file.
This means all users will likely have to update their inputs files. All
inputs files in IAMR/Exec/run2d, run3d, eb_run2d, eb_run3d, and
run_2d_particles have been updated, and can serve as examples. The Users'
Guide has also been updated.

Also includes bug fix for non-EB problems run on the GPU, and a temporary
revert of replacing Elixirs with The_Async_Arena (3a15e4e0d18d0bddf0f32ad64dfb75393e844574)

To summarize changes to inputs file:
1. Constant Dirichlet boundary conditions are now specified in the inputs
   file, e.g.  xlo.velocity = 1. 0. 0.  specifies a velocity of (1, 0, 0)
   at the low x face of the domain.
2. Refinement criteria is now specified using refinement indicators (see
   Users Guide section 6.1.1 or examples in IAMR/Exec)
3. Unused probtypes/problem initialization setups have been removed. If I
   removed something in error, please let me know and it will be put back.

author: Weiqun Zhang <weiqunzhang@lbl.gov>
commit message:
Simplify cache cleanup actions

In our old approach, a workflow file contains a job that uploads the PR
number as an artifact. While the PR is still open, the workflow_run
triggered by it will download the artifact and use the information to clean
up all except the last used cache associated with that original
workflow. When a PR is merged or closed, there will be a post-pr workflow
that uploads the PR number as an artifact and triggers a workflow_run that
clean up all caches associated with the PR. The reason we did it this way
was in the cache cleanup workflows, we did not find an easy way to get the
number of the PR triggering them. This is not convenient because we have to
add jobs uploading artifacts to workflow files.

After some experiments, we have found a reliable way to find the PR number
without using artifacts. The workflow_run's payload always contains the head
SHA of the commit that triggers it, whether the PR comes from a fork or
not. We can then use `gh pr list` to search for that head and obtain the PR
number.

Added ParmParse variable num_steps.  The basic idea is to tell the program
to run num_steps more steps from wherever you restart.  It works by
setting max_step.  If max_step < 0 it just sets max_step to the current
step + num_steps.  Otherwise it sets max_step to the minimum of max_step
and the sum of current step + num_steps.

Fix MAC sync for certain Godunov cases.

During the MAC sync, we need to reconstruct the edge states exactly
as we made them during the advection step of advance. This was not
happening correctly for the scalars when using Godunov with divU!=0
or, for divU=0, non-conservative scalars.

This does not affect the mac_sync_comute version where edge states
are saved and not recomputed.

commit message:
Update create umac grown (#117)

Make new NSB::create_umac_grown that uses FillPatchTwoLevels.

This fixes an error wherein the valid fine face values at the coarse-fine interface were not being used in the computation of some fine ghost cell values. Previously, IAMR used HydroUtils::create_constrained_umac_grown which relies on InterpFromCoarseLevel (which uses interpolated coarse values at the coarse-fine interface rather than the valid fine data that exists there in this case). Differences are likely subtle, as create_constrained_umac_grown makes further corrections after the interpolation.

commit message:
Eliminated the array is_conservative() in favor of two arrays advectionType()
and diffusionType() which control the form of the advection terms and the
diffusive terms.  The new arrays are of the types, Array<AdvectionForm> and
Array<DiffusionForm>, respectively.  AdvectionForm and DiffusionForm are
enumerations defined in Godunov.H and Diffusion.H.  AdvectionForm will
take the values Conservative and NonConservative and DiffusionForm will
take the values RhoInverse_Laplacian_S = 0, Laplacian_SoverRho, and
Laplacian_S.

commit message:
Fix mac sync (#118)

Fix MAC sync for certain Godunov cases.

During the MAC sync, we need to reconstruct the edge states exactly
as we made them during the advection step of advance. This was not
happening correctly for the scalars when using Godunov with divU!=0
or, for divU=0, non-conservative scalars.

This does not affect the mac_sync_comute version where edge states
are saved and not recomputed.

author: Brian Friesen <bfriesen@lbl.gov>
commit message:
NS_util: move OpenMP user-defined reduction machinery outside namespace

If this UDR is defined inside the 'amrex' namespace, the Cray compiler
complains that it is incompletely defined. If it is moved outside the
namespace, then the compiler is happy.  Intel did not complain about this
either way.

I don't see anything in the OpenMP spec that says whether this is right or
wrong. The closest thing I could find is in section 2.16 of the OpenMP 4.5
spec, which says

  The declare reduction directive can also appear at points in the program at
  which a static data member could be declared. In this case, the visibility and
  accessibility of the declaration are the same as those of a static data member
  declared at the same point in the program.

I will submit this test case to Cray to find out if they think the compiler is
correct or if it is a compiler bug.

commit message:
Remove NSB::do_scalar_update_in_order.

Commits 895d3dec and 5765ae03 effectively nullified this option.
This option's implementation created a subtle problem for the
default case (where do_scalar_update_in_order = 0), in that before
the advective update, S_new actually holds S^(n-1) (and this is
because NSB::advance_setup does a swap and thus puts S^(n-1) in
S_new and S^n in S_old).

If the functionality of do_scalar_update_in_order is still needed,
please open an issue on github.

author: lijewski <mjlijewski@lbl.gov>
commit message:
Reverting to simpler version of multByBndryMask().  Compared to
copyPerioidic() and incrementPeriodic(), the communication pattern is
quite expensive to calculate for very large numbers of Boxes.  Experiments
have proven to me that it's ultimately cheaper to use CollectData() to
collectively calculate the communication pattern, than to have each CPU
calculate the full pattern.  Unless this function was called so often that
it was worth cacheing the pattern.  Then it would beat CollectData().  But
since it's not called often enough (the patterns aren't repeated
enough) to justify cacheing, the fancy way is a lose.

of bcoefs. These Infs will creep into the MLMG solver.

author: Weiqun Zhang <WeiqunZhang@lbl.gov>
commit message:
Simplify cache cleanup actions (#168)

In our old approach, a workflow file contains a job that uploads the PR
number as an artifact. While the PR is still open, the workflow_run
triggered by it will download the artifact and use the information to
clean up all except the last used cache associated with that original
workflow. When a PR is merged or closed, there will be a post-pr
workflow that uploads the PR number as an artifact and triggers a
workflow_run that clean up all caches associated with the PR. The reason
we did it this way was in the cache cleanup workflows, we did not find
an easy way to get the number of the PR triggering them. This is not
convenient because we have to add jobs uploading artifacts to workflow
files.

After some experiments, we have found a reliable way to find the PR
number without using artifacts. The workflow_run's payload always
contains the head SHA of the commit that triggers it, whether the PR
comes from a fork or not. We can then use `gh pr list` to search for
that head and obtain the PR number.

author: almgren <almgren>
commit message:
Yet another fix to FORT_ESTATE_FPU in GODUNOV*.F.
  1) we now check in Godunov.cpp to see whether velpred == 1.  We are only allowed
     to call FORT_ESTATE_FPU for velpred = 0.  Code which does velpred=1 case
     in FORT_ESTATE_FPU is removed.
  2) Tests on whether uedge(i,j)*uedge(i+1,j) .lt. 0 has been changed to .le. 0
     to correctly capture that case (equivalently for other directions).
  3) For iconserv = 1, have modified the way the transverse term is constructed,
     so as to not create bad values on the ghost cells of fine grids which have come
     from coarse grid interpolation.  There u_x + v_y != divu, so we modify the
     transverse terms with a correction +(u_x + v_y - divu), which is the MAC tolerance
     for all interior fine cells, but nontrivial for ghost cells.  This is done
     by putting the divu term back into the tforces term (with a negative sign),
     and then adding s(u_x + v_y) into the transverse term.

commit message:
Simplify cache cleanup actions

For the CleanUpCache workflow run triggered by PR workflows, there is a
simple way of getting the PR number. The full event webhook payload is
available as a json file and it contains the number of the triggering PR. So
we don't need to upload the PR number as an artifact.

For the post-PR cleanup, we could also clean up the cache directly without
uploading the PR number and triggering a workflow run for cleaning.

commit message:
TLS migration for demos/web (#260)

What does this PR do?

Minimally invasive migration to TLS for the http (8000) and websocket (9000) endpoints for the real time web demo.

Where should the reviewer start?

Install the demo like a normal install. During the install-deps.sh script it will prompt for questions to generate a local self-signed cert. Anything can be entered into the cert. Start the demo as normal but connect on https://domain:http_port instead of http.

How should this PR be tested?

The first step is the cert generation (added to install-deps.sh for convenience). The second step is ensuring the two endpoints are brought up. The next step is loading the web page and accepting the self-signed cert. Reloading the web app everything should now be secure, e.g. no errors or warnings and the video works as normal.

Any background context you want to provide?

I tried to be as minimal as possible so the changes tends to follow the existing structure rather than a refactor of anything major. With that said, SimpleHTTPServer doesn't work with TLS via the -m flag so that is now a short script. I updated all the html/js files to point to https/wss. I also updated the js for Firefox's change from navigator.mozGetUserMedia to navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia.

What are the relevant issues?

#75

Questions:

Do the docs need to be updated?
Yes. I updated the script's docs in demos/web but didn't make any changes outside of demos/web

Does this PR add new (Python) dependencies?
I don't think so.

commit message:
TLS migration for demos/web

What does this PR do?

Minimally invasive migration to TLS for the http (8000) and websocket (9000) endpoints for the real time web demo.

Where should the reviewer start?

Install the demo like a normal install. During the install-deps.sh script it will prompt for questions to generate a local self-signed cert. Anything can be entered into the cert. Start the demo as normal but connect on https://domain:http_port instead of http.

How should this PR be tested?

The first step is the cert generation (added to install-deps.sh for convenience). The second step is ensuring the two endpoints are brought up. The next step is loading the web page and accepting the self-signed cert. Reloading the web app everything should now be secure, e.g. no errors or warnings and the video works as normal.

Any background context you want to provide?

I tried to be as minimal as possible so the changes tends to follow the existing structure rather than a refactor of anything major. With that said, SimpleHTTPServer doesn't work with TLS via the -m flag so that is now a short script. I updated all the html/js files to point to https/wss. I also updated the js for Firefox's change from navigator.mozGetUserMedia to navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia.

What are the relevant issues?

#75

Questions:

Do the docs need to be updated?
Yes. I updated the script's docs in demos/web but didn't make any changes outside of demos/web

Does this PR add new (Python) dependencies?
I don't think so.

commit message:
Refine AnnoTALE CLI packaging

- Replace hard-coded macOS paths in projects/xanthogenomes/AnnoTALEcli.xml with repo-relative properties.
- Load Jstacs classes from dist/jstacs-2.5.jar instead of the temporary tempbin dir. Keep explicit library list and existing exclusions.

Run:
```
ant -Dbuilddir=$(pwd)/dist buildjar
ant -f projects/xanthogenomes/AnnoTALEcli.xml
```

If the core jar lives elsewhere, run the second command with
`... -Djstacs.jar=/path/to/jstacs-2.5.jar`.

From [here](https://github.com/richelbilderbeek/R-CodingStandard/blob/master/R-CodingStandard.md#br4-prefer-to-surround-else-with-braces-12) I collected these references:

    [1] Google's R Style Guide: Surround else with braces. An else statement should always be surrounded on the same line by curly braces.
    [2] 'R Style. An Rchaeological Commentary.' by Paul E. Johnson, February 13, 2015, 3.4 (SEA .70) The "} else {" policy
    [3] 'R packages' by Hadley Wickham, O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2015, Chapter 3, paragraph 'Curly braces': A closing curly brace should always go on its own line, unless it's followed by else

Merge branch 'master' into fix-windows-build

* master: (46 commits)
  fix examples to work with required message argument of snapshot create
  rearrange test_snapshot_private and add tests for _file_setup

  convert config and stats default to {} to match assumption in other parts of code
  added params to docstrings for private functions
  normalize file open command with `from io import open` and ensure unicode to enable python 2/3 compatibility
  fix small tweaks to improve code quality in codacy
  added more info to entity docstrings to explain constraints and better explain all parameters, attributes, and methods (if present)
  added new client Task object and include ability to get file objects from the Task object + tests
  update core Task entity to have duration as a float of seconds
  added new logic for new attributes of task + added get_files function to return a list of file objects for the task + tests
  handle None values for datetime start_time and end_time objects.
  add handling for start_time and end_time datetime objects in storage code and tests to verify
  added directory support for get() function for file driver
  clean docstrings to match standard numpy / scipy format
  update FileDriver abstract class and local driver to add get and get_collection_files functions to retrieve file objects
  added duration to entity and changed container_id to run_id
  fix docstrings in blitzdbdriver code to match numpy / scipy style
  added new variables to core task entity and added tests
  fixed naming and spacing for test files

commit message:
Create publish.yml

This GitHub Action builds wheels and sdists and pushes them to GitHub's releases page and PyPI. All you have to do is go to [New Release](https://github.com/voxelmorph/voxelmorph/releases/new), fill in a version tag like "v0.9.1", click Publish, and a couple minutes later the .whl and .tar.gz will be up on [Releases](https://github.com/voxelmorph/voxelmorph/releases) and on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/voxelmorph).

To get PyPI working as well, [get a PyPI token](https://pypi.org/manage/account/token/), give it to GitHub [here](https://github.com/voxelmorph/voxelmorph/settings/secrets/actions) named `PYPI_TOKEN`.

Fixes https://github.com/voxelmorph/voxelmorph/issues/432
